intelligence.enrichment: When vegetation becomes scarce and waterholes dry up in a natural habitat, animals may move into farms and villages in search of resources. Loss of forest cover and changed rainfall can reduce food and water in the natural habitat, causing movement toward human-used areas. The learner correctly applies this rule: When vegetation becomes scarce and waterholes dry up in a natural habitat, animals may move into farms and villages in search of resources. Elephants enter villages because they prefer human crops, not because the forest no longer supports them.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Ecosystems and habitats.
